blocks.content: GOVERNOR

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Governor is the constitutional (nominal) head of a State, while real executive power lies with the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
The Governor is appointed by the President under Article 155 and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
To be eligible, a person must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age; no educational qualifications are prescribed.
The Governor occupies a dual position as the constitutional head of the State and the representative of the Union Government.
Judicial powers include granting pardons, reprieves, or remissions, but the Governor cannot pardon a death sentence.
INTRODUCTION

blocks.content: The Governor is the constitutional head of a State in India. He occupies a position similar to that of the President at the Centre.
While the President represents the Union, the Governor represents the State.
The office of the Governor is established under Part VI of the Indian Constitution (Articles 153 to 167).
The Governor acts as a vital link between the Union Government and the State Government.
Although the Governor is the nominal head of the State, the real executive power is exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
APPOINTMENT OF THE GOVERNOR
The Governor is appointed by the President of India under Article 155. Important points regarding appointment:

items:
• Governor is not elected directly or indirectly.
  • He is appointed by the President on the advice of the Central Government.
  • The Governor acts as the representative of the President in the State.
  • One person can be appointed Governor of more than one State.
Governor is not elected directly or indirectly.
He is appointed by the President on the advice of the Central Government.
The Governor acts as the representative of the President in the State.
One person can be appointed Governor of more than one State.

blocks.content: QUALIFICATIONS OF THE GOVERNOR
To be appointed as a Governor, a person must:

items:
• Be a citizen of India
  • Have completed 35 years of age
Be a citizen of India
Have completed 35 years of age

blocks.content: There are no educational qualifications prescribed in the Constitution.
CONDITIONS OF GOVERNOR’S OFFICE
To ensure independence of the Governor, the Constitution lays down certain conditions:

items:
• The Governor shall not be a member of Parliament or State Legislature.
  • He shall not hold any office of profit.
  • His salary and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
  • His official residence is Raj Bhavan.
The Governor shall not be a member of Parliament or State Legislature.
He shall not hold any office of profit.
His salary and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
His official residence is Raj Bhavan.

blocks.content: TERM OF OFFICE
The Governor holds office for a term of five years. However:

items:
• He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
  • He may resign by submitting resignation to the President.
  • He can be removed before the completion of his term.
He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
He may resign by submitting resignation to the President.
He can be removed before the completion of his term.

blocks.content: Thus, the Governor does not enjoy a fixed tenure.

blocks.content: EXECUTIVE POWERS
The executive authority of the State is vested in the Governor. His executive powers include:

items:
• Appointment of Chief Minister
  • Appointment of Council of Ministers on advice of CM
  • Appointment of Advocate General
  • Appointment of State Election Commissioner and members of State PSC
  • All executive actions of the State are taken in the name of the Governor
Appointment of Chief Minister

blocks.content: LEGISLATIVE POWERS
The Governor is an integral part of the State Legislature. His legislative powers include:

items:
• Summoning, proroguing and dissolving the State Legislature
  • Addressing the first session of State Legislature
  • Nominating members to Legislative Council (if exists)
  • Giving assent to Bills
  • Reserving Bills for the consideration of the President
  • Promulgating Ordinances under Article 213

blocks.content: FINANCIAL POWERS
The Governor plays an important role in State finances:

items:
• Money Bill can be introduced only with his recommendation
  • State Budget is presented in his name
  • He constitutes the State Finance Commission
  • He controls the Contingency Fund of the State
Money Bill can be introduced only with his recommendation

blocks.content: JUDICIAL POWERS
The Governor has certain judicial powers:

items:
• He appoints District Judges in consultation with the High Court
  • He has the power to grant pardon, reprieve, respite or remission of punishment
  • He cannot pardon death sentence (only President can)
He appoints District Judges in consultation with the High Court
He has the power to grant pardon, reprieve, respite or remission of punishment
He cannot pardon death sentence (only President can)

blocks.content: DISCRETIONARY POWERS OF THE GOVERNOR
The Governor has certain discretionary powers which he can exercise independently. These include:

items:
• Appointment of Chief Minister when no party has clear majority
  • Dismissal of Council of Ministers
  • Dissolution of Legislative Assembly
  • Reservation of Bill for President‟s consideration
  • Recommending President‟s Rule under Article 356
Appointment of Chief Minister when no party has clear majority
Dismissal of Council of Ministers
Dissolution of Legislative Assembly
Reservation of Bill for President‟s consideration
Recommending President‟s Rule under Article 356

blocks.content: These powers make the Governor a powerful constitutional authority.
GOVERNOR AND PRESIDENT’S RULE
Under Article 356, the Governor can recommend President‟s Rule in a State if:

items:
• Constitutional machinery fails
  • Government cannot be run according to Constitution
Constitutional machinery fails
Government cannot be run according to Constitution

blocks.content: This is often called „State Emergency‟.
The Governor plays a crucial role in such situations.
POSITION OF GOVERNOR
The Governor occupies a dual position:

items:
• Constitutional head of the State
  • Representative of the Union Government
Constitutional head of the State
Representative of the Union Government

blocks.content: This dual role often leads to controversy regarding misuse of powers.
GOVERNOR VS CHIEF MINISTER
Governor:

items:
• Appointed by President
  • Nominal executive
  • Acts mostly on advice
Appointed by President
Nominal executive
Acts mostly on advice
Death Sentence Exception: The Governor has the power to grant pardons and remissions, but CANNOT pardon a death sentence (exclusive to the President).
Ordinance Power: Governor's power to promulgate ordinances comes under Article 213.
Tenure: The Governor does NOT enjoy a fixed tenure and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
Key Landmark Cases: Shamsher Singh Case (Governor as constitutional head), Rameshwar Prasad Case (Misuse of Art 356), and SR Bommai Case (Limits on Governor's power).

blocks.content: CONCLUSION
The Governor plays a crucial role in the constitutional framework of India.
Although he is a nominal head, his discretionary powers give him significant influence in State politics.
The office of Governor must function with neutrality and constitutional morality to maintain the federal balance of India.
